accuracy.evidence: Checked against the AQA A-level Chemistry specification 3.3.6.2 and its data sheet (C–H 2850–3300, O–H alcohol 3230–3550, C=O 1680–1750, C–O 1000–1300 cm⁻¹), OCR A 4.2.4(c) on IR absorption by CO₂, H₂O and CH₄, the NIST Chemistry WebBook (CO stretch 2143 cm⁻¹; CO₂ fundamentals 667 bend, 1388 symmetric stretch IR-inactive, 2349 asymmetric stretch) and LibreTexts 'Infrared spectroscopy' (harmonic oscillator ν̃ = (1/2πc)√(k/μ) and the selection rule that the dipole moment must change). The lab's model wavenumbers use 1303√(k/μ) with k in mdyn/Å and μ in u: C–H 3030, C–D 2230, C–Cl 800, C–O 1110, C=O 1710, C≡O 2150 cm⁻¹, each inside the data-book range shown beside it. Air shares (N₂ 78%, O₂ 21%, Ar about 0.9%, CO₂ about 0.04%, CH₄ about 0.0002%, water vapour variable up to about 4%) follow NOAA. Parameterised answers (n, 50n, 200n, 10n) were enumerated by the validator and use only + − × so the app can evaluate them.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented A-level slips (RSC Education 'Spectroscopy in a suitcase' teacher notes; Taber's Chemical misconceptions on bonding and energy): longer bonds absorb at higher wavenumber (step 2 predict, tag longer), mass does not matter if the bond is the same (step 1 predict, tags heavier and massnot), all IR is absorbed or high energy is what counts (step 3 predict, tags all and highest), IR breaks bonds or moves electrons (tags breaks and electron), N₂ does not absorb because its bond is strong (step 4 predict, tag strong), only polar molecules absorb (CO₂ bend and asymmetric stretch in the sort; m2), and N₂ is too rare to matter (tag rare).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed. 413 Identifying compounds with instrumental analysis reads IR spectra by matching bands to groups, and 754 The molecular ion peak covers mass spectra; neither models why a band sits where it does. Only this lab animates ball-and-spring bonds whose plucked frequency comes from √(k/μ), scans an IR source across a transmittance trace to find resonance, sorts vibrations by dipole change, and builds up greenhouse absorbers in a column of air.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each rule before it is stated: plucking C–H, C–D and C–Cl shows the number fall as the atom gets heavier; plucking C–O, C=O and C≡O shows it rise with bond order; sweeping the IR source shows the trace dip only near 1710 cm⁻¹ and the bond swinging harder only there; sorting the seven vibrations shows the pattern (same-atom and symmetric stretches inactive); adding gases shows N₂, O₂ and Ar change nothing while CO₂, H₂O and CH₄ stop IR. Banners state the rule only after the task is won.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'It stays the same: it is still one bond' for C–H to C–Cl, 'C–O, the longest bond' and 'All the same: same atoms' for the highest wavenumber, 'All of it equally' and 'Only the highest wavenumbers' for what C=O absorbs, and 'Yes, strong bonds absorb the most' for N₂. Each is disproved by the task that follows, and the task message reports whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with twelve tagged wrong answers, each with its own message: longer, same (bond strength), heavier, massnot (reduced mass), strong, gas (dipole change not bond strength or state), all, highest (resonance), heavy, rare (greenhouse gases), electron, breaks (what IR does to a bond). Correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Learner text scores Flesch-Kincaid 3.1 (limit 6.5) and adult text 7.6 (limit 9.5) while keeping the precise terms covalent bond, natural frequency, wavenumber, force constant, reduced mass, vibrational energy level, dipole and greenhouse gas. The formula appears only in the key idea and adult text; learners meet it through the spring picture.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson. Each learner paragraph adds one idea (spring model, strength and mass, quantised absorption, dipole rule and greenhouse gases); the adult text gives the specification points, the lab sequence and the specific mistakes.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in dark and light themes before and after Show me at every step (/workspace/wn2353-shots/ir-*). Fixes made from them: the transmittance panel was shortened so the axis title clears the feedback box, the sorted vibrations now list inside their bins and the bins grow as cards are sorted, the greenhouse arrows start above the ground label and the status line was shortened so it is not clipped. Bond rows, the IR knob (36 px target plus a full-width drag track) and gas tiles are readable and reachable.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13 with axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes and no console errors. Every drag has a button: Pluck C–H and the rest, −500/−50/+50/+500 cm⁻¹ for the IR source, Pick then IR active or inactive, Add gas. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the wavenumbers, source position, vibrations left or gases added, and the oscillation stops under reduced motion.
